addSources.institution: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
addSources.title: OECD Guidelines on the Protection of Privacy and Transborder Flows of Personal Data (2002 edition, with the 1980 Explanatory Memorandum)
addSources.quote: There should be a general policy of openness about developments, practices and policies with respect to personal data. Means should be readily available of establishing the existence and nature of personal data, and the main purposes of their use, as well as the identity and usual residence of the data controller.
addSources.note: Checked with fetch-text.py --check: FOUND. Annex, Part Two ('PART TWO. BASIC PRINCIPLES OF NATIONAL APPLICATION', FOUND), heading 'Openness Principle', para. 12. The paragraph number '12.' sits on its own line in the PDF text layer, so the quote starts at 'There should be'. The 2013 revision (OECD/LEGAL/0188, legalinstruments.oecd.org) keeps para. 12 word for word.

issues: The 'text' is not the Guidelines' wording as published. In the OECD's own edition, sub-paragraph (b) has four numbered items, 'i) within a reasonable time; ii) at a charge, if any, that is not excessive; iii) in a reasonable manner; and iv) in a form that is readily intelligible to him;'. The record drops the numerals, and it prints 'subparagraphs(a)' where the original has 'subparagraphs (a)'. Both are transcription slips, probably from the HTML page, and are corrected in 'text'. The substance was right.

Name, year 1980, order 7 and source date 1980-09-23 are correct. The note ('revised in 2013; this is the 1980 text') is right and matters here. The 2013 revision changed para. 13 to gender-neutral wording ('Individuals should have the right: ... relating to them'; legalinstruments.oecd.org OECD/LEGAL/0188, FOUND), and 'relating to him' is NO-MATCH there.
The only source (a Wayback copy) could not be re-fetched and is set to PENDING. The OECD 2002 edition PDF is added as a confirmed source.

fieldFixes.text: 13. An individual should have the right: a) to obtain from a data controller, or otherwise, confirmation of whether or not the data controller has data relating to him; b) to have communicated to him, data relating to him i) within a reasonable time; ii) at a charge, if any, that is not excessive; iii) in a reasonable manner; and iv) in a form that is readily intelligible to him; c) to be given reasons if a request made under subparagraphs (a) and (b) is denied, and to be able to challenge such denial; and d) to challenge data relating to him and, if the challenge is successful to have the data erased, rectified, completed or amended.
